keyFindings.description: The deferral cap does not bound what its comment claims, by two independent mechanisms. (a) listenerDeliveryHandler draws a fresh *atomic.Int64 whenever its caller set none (delivery.go:296-299), and main.go builds a handler three times - coreNATSDeliveryHandler at :767, jetStreamDeliveryHandler at :804, and again at :890 on the self-health rebind - so a durable rebound after a NATS flap, the event this whole change is about, opens a second 64-slot budget while the previous handler's deferrals still hold their slots. (b) releaseDeferredUnplaceable fires on every agent-lane redelivery with NumDelivered > 1 (delivery.go:626-631), including redeliveries this handler never deferred: an interest-path ShouldNAK's 30 s NAK (handler.go:90 -> delivery.go:808-810), publishNoHolderExceptionOrNak's NAK (delivery.go:282), and an expired AckWait (durable.go:29). Those correlate with deferrals, since a session whose server is down produces both, so the count can sit at zero while the handler holds its full cap and more. delivery.go:588-595 states (b) and argues the 192-slot distance to consumerMaxAckPending absorbs it; the over-release is unbounded, so that argument does not carry. Remedy: one counter set once in main.go's deliveryConfig with the nil default removed, and a deferred set keyed on metadata.Sequence.Stream (or dedupe key plus session) so only slots this handler took are released.

outcomePublishDenied's comment says 'Both message routes can record it'. The send route publishes to contracts.AgentSubject(target), notifications.agent.<id>, which internal/bus/stream.go:77 lists in streamSubjects, so usesCoreTransport is false and the publish goes through publishJetStream; bus.ErrPublishDenied is produced only at internal/bus/confirm.go:106, reached only from publishCoreTo. The send route therefore cannot record it. publish_refusal_answers_test.go drives both routes through refuseBusUnavailable with a constructed error and says in its own doc that it pins the answer rather than the detection, so nothing contradicts this - only the comment does. Same class as round one's finding at delivery.go:681.

The replacement for round one's unreachable-path comment cites another unreachable path: session.ReasonNone is said to be reached by ErrWrongMachine, and docs/architecture.md:116 carries the same row, but no production code returns ErrWrongMachine - the sole producer is internal/integration/e2e_test.go:355. So placementMayChange is always true in production and the no_push_target label-sharing describes nothing that happens.

A push_failed delivery is retried with its attempt-cache entry cleared and no dedupe entry recorded, and session.prompt (internal/session/session.go:154-184) returns the same error for a refusal and for an answer lost after the session server took the prompt, so a push that landed can be repeated up to thirteen times. The interest path already behaved this way (clearAttempt: result.ShouldNAK, delivery.go:689), so this round widens an existing gap rather than opening one - but it follows from the branch round one asked for and belongs on the record as a decision, not a side effect.

GET /v1/roles/<role> still answers a lost role-claim CAS race 500 with the old text, now that errRoleHolderChanged exists to tell it apart from a read that did not answer. Pre-existing route, outside this diff's behaviour change; named as a fast-follow rather than a finding.
